# fivenines_smart_devices (Data Source)

smartctl's PASSED / FAILED verdict per drive -- the half of disk health that no metrics query carries. The wear percentage is queryable as `disk_health_percentage`; the VERDICT is state, and a drive can report 100% life remaining and FAILED on the same tick.

A NULL `overall_health` MEANS SMARTCTL GAVE NO VERDICT, not PASSED: a drive behind a RAID controller that passes no SMART through, or a USB bridge that does not implement it. `verdict_known` is published beside it so a `failed = false` never has to carry "or we could not tell" -- read it first.

These are SNAPSHOT ENTRIES, not rows: no stable id and no timestamps. Use `collector.last_reported_at` for freshness.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "fivenines_smart_devices" "all" {
  instance_id = fivenines_instance.db.id
}

output "failing_drives" {
  value = [for d in data.fivenines_smart_devices.all.smart_devices : d.device if d.failed]
}

# Read verdict_known before failed: a null overall_health means smartctl gave
# NO verdict (RAID controller, USB bridge), never PASSED. Without this,
# "failed = false" quietly means "healthy, or we could not tell".
output "drives_with_no_verdict" {
  value = [
    for d in data.fivenines_smart_devices.all.smart_devices :
    d.device if !d.verdict_known
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID the rows belong to.

### Optional

- `health` (String) THREE values, not two: `unknown` is a real state (smartctl reported no verdict) and a two-valued filter would force it into one of the other buckets. One of: `passed`, `failed`, `unknown`.
- `q` (String) Case-insensitive substring match on the device name.

### Read-Only

- `collector` (Attributes) Why the row list looks the way it does. Read this before treating an empty list as a clean bill of health: `[]` alone cannot distinguish "this host genuinely runs none" from "the collector is switched off" (which deletes the rows) or "this agent is too old to report them". (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--collector))
- `smart_devices` (Attributes List) The rows the collector reported. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--smart_devices))

<a id="nestedatt--collector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `collector`

Read-Only:

- `blocked_reason` (String) The agent's own explanation, where it sent one. Null otherwise.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the operator has this collector switched on for the instance. Switching it off deletes the rows, so `false` fully explains an empty list.
- `last_reported_at` (String) The instance's last agent check-in -- not this collector's. It separates "this collector went quiet" (rows stale, instance reporting) from "the whole agent went quiet" (both). Per-row freshness is each row's `last_synced_at`.
- `name` (String) The collector these rows come from.
- `pending` (Boolean) Enabled, and the agent knows the feature, but the capability is not satisfied yet (missing binary, missing permission). The rows are legitimately absent and may appear on a later tick.
- `supported` (Boolean) Whether this agent can collect these rows -- its own capability verdict where it reports one, its version otherwise. `false` alongside `enabled` means the instance was asked for something it cannot deliver. Read it as "the agent has not said it cannot": the config-driven collectors (haproxy, rabbitmq, php_fpm, wireguard) have no version floor, so an agent predating one still reports `true` with an empty list.
- `unavailable_reason` (String) Why `supported` is false: `host_lacks_feature` (the agent probed and reported it cannot) or `agent_outdated` (the agent predates the release that collects these rows). Null when supported.


<a id="nestedatt--smart_devices"></a>
### Nested Schema for `smart_devices`

Read-Only:

- `device` (String) The device node, e.g. `/dev/sda`. The natural key; these entries carry no id.
- `failed` (Boolean) The verdict is FAILED. False when unknown -- see `verdict_known`.
- `overall_health` (String) smartctl's own word, normalized to PASSED / FAILED where the line was recognized and carried verbatim where it was not. NULL MEANS SMARTCTL GAVE NO VERDICT -- a drive behind a RAID controller that passes no SMART through, or a USB bridge that does not implement it. It does NOT mean PASSED, and that is the one misreading this endpoint exists to prevent.
- `passed` (Boolean) The verdict is PASSED. False when unknown -- see `verdict_known`.
- `verdict_known` (Boolean) Whether `overall_health` carries a verdict at all. Read this before `failed`: without it, `failed: false` silently means "healthy, or we could not tell".
